'''Nando Bruno Alfred Andre de Colo''' (born 23 June 1987)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Türkiye Basketbol Federasyonu|url=https://www.tbf.org.tr/ligler/bsl-2019-2020/basketbolcu-detay/473100|access-date=2020-10-28|website=tbf.org.tr|language=tr}}</ref> is a French former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at a height of {{height|ft=6|in=5}}, he played at the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions. A six-time [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague]] selection, de Colo won the EuroLeague title in [[2015–16 Euroleague|2016]] and [[2018–19 Euroleague|2019]] with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], earning both the [[EuroLeague MVP]] and [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP|Final Four MVP]] awards in the process.

De Colo is the all-time top scorer in European continental basketball competitions, having surpassed [[Nikos Galis]] in 2022.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-02-06 |title=France's De Colo achieves legendary status as top scorer in European club competitions history |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/news/frances-de-colo-achieves-legendary-status-as-top-scorer-in-european-club-competitions-history |access-date=2023-02-07 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
De Colo was born in [[Sainte-Catherine-lès-Arras]], France to parents who were both born and raised in [[Portugal]]. He attended Lycée Fernand Renaudeau in [[Cholet]], and made his first appearance on the [[Cholet Basket|Cholet Under-20 team]] in 2004–05.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lyc-renaudeau-49.ac-nantes.fr/spip.php?article771|title=Un ancien élève en NBA|date=25 June 2009|publisher=Lycée Fernand Renaudeau|access-date=13 May 2013|archive-date=28 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131228093752/http://lyc-renaudeau-49.ac-nantes.fr/spip.php?article771|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Cholet Basket (2006–2009)===
De Colo made his professional debut during the 2006–07 season with [[Cholet Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]]. Under supervision of head coach [[Erman Kunter]], he helped the team win the 2008 [[Semaine des As]] (French A Leaders Cup) and reach the finals of the 2008 [[French Basketball Cup|French Cup]] and of the [[2008–09 FIBA EuroChallenge|2009 EuroChallenge]].

On 1 June 2009, he parted ways with Cholet.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/77128/de-colo-left-cholet.html De Colo left Cholet]</ref> On 25 June 2009, he was selected with the 53rd overall pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]].

===Valencia (2009–2012)===
On 13 July 2009, he signed a three-year deal with [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] of Spain.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/eurocup/78044/de-colo-is-now-a-valencia-player.html De Colo is now a Valencia player]</ref> He went on to win the [[2009–10 Eurocup Basketball|2010 EuroCup title]] with Valencia and selected [[EuroCup Basketball All-EuroCup Team|All-EuroCup First Team]].

===San Antonio Spurs (2012–2014)===
On 10 July 2012, De Colo announced he would not be re-signing with Valencia in order to play in the NBA.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/93330/nando-de-colo-leaves-valencia-for-the-spurs.html Nando De Colo leaves Valencia for the Spurs]</ref> On 13 July 2012, he signed a two-year deal with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10506 |title=Spurs sign guard Nando De Colo |access-date=11 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203011555/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10506 |archive-date=3 December 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During his rookie and sophomore seasons, he had multiple assignments with the [[Austin Toros]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]]. De Colo reached the [[2013 NBA Finals]] with the Spurs, but the team lost to the [[Miami Heat]] in seven games.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html 2012–13 NBA Assignments] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |date=27 March 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |title=2013–14 NBA Assignments |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=27 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703151241/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |archive-date=3 July 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2014)===
On 20 February 2014, De Colo was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Austin Daye]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-acquire-nando-de-colo/ |title=Raptors Acquire Nando De Colo |access-date=21 February 2014 |archive-date=24 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224181900/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-acquire-nando-de-colo/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===CSKA Moscow (2014–2019)===
On 9 July 2014, De Colo signed a two-year deal (with the third year being optional) with the Russian club [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=CSKA Moscow snags De Colo on two-year deal|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138493|work=Euroleague.net|date=9 July 2014|access-date=11 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nando De Colo has become the first Frenchman in CSKA history|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=13605&lang=en|work=cskabasket.com|date=9 July 2014|access-date=11 July 2014}}</ref> In May 2015, he was chosen to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]], for his performances over the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5xtj7vjfuokfw7g8|access-date=8 May 2015|work=euroleague.net}}</ref>

In the 2014–15 season, CSKA Moscow managed to advance to the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four|EuroLeague Final Four]], for the fourth straight season, after eliminating [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] for the second straight season in the [[2014–15 Euroleague Quarter-finals|EuroLeague quarterfinals]] playoffs series, with a 3–1 series victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow routs Panathinaikos to claim Final Four berth|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=246&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=18 May 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=22 April 2015}}</ref> However, in the EuroLeague Final Four's semi-final game, despite being dubbed by the media as an absolute favorite to advance to the Finals, CSKA once again lost to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. The final score was 70–68, after a great Olympiacos comeback in the 4th quarter, which was led by [[Vassilis Spanoulis]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Spanoulis comes through again as Olympiacos stuns CSKA|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=249&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=18 May 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=15 May 2015}}</ref> CSKA Moscow eventually won the third place game, after defeating [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]], by a score of 86–80.<ref>{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow beats Fenerbahce in third-place game|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=18 May 2015|work=eurolague.net|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> In his second EuroLeague season, De Colo averaged a career-high 14.4 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game, over 28 games played. On 21 May 2015, De Colo won the [[VTB United League MVP]] Award.<ref>[http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/nando-de-colo-named-regular-season-mvp.htm Nando de Colo named regular season MVP] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150522133937/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/nando-de-colo-named-regular-season-mvp.htm |date=22 May 2015 }}</ref> CSKA Moscow finished the season by winning the [[2014–15 VTB United League|VTB United League]] championship, after eliminating [[BC Khimki|Khimki]], with a 3–0 series sweep in the league's finals series.<ref>{{cite news|title=CSKA wins championship!|url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-wins-championship.htm|access-date=10 June 2015|work=vtb-league.com|date=8 June 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610135415/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-wins-championship.htm|archive-date=10 June 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

On 3 May 2016, De Colo was awarded with the [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy]], an annual award given to the EuroLeague's top scorer of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=2015–16 Alphonso Ford Top Scorer Trophy: Nando De Colo, CSKA Moscow|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6uv4mhcmasjkj9yf|access-date=3 May 2016|work=Euroleague.net|date=3 May 2016}}</ref> Nine days later, he was named the [[EuroLeague MVP]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6vm3u6fokf8svf56|title=2015–16 Euroleague MVP: Nando De Colo, CSKA Moscow|work=Euroleague.net|date=12 May 2016|access-date=16 May 2016}}</ref> On 15 May, CSKA won the EuroLeague title, and De Colo was named the [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP]].<ref>{{cite news|title=De Colo celebrates title as Final Four MVP|url=http://www.euroleague.net/final-four/berlin-2016/news/i/6vv9xlr95xxqfeoh/de-colo-celebrates-title-as-final-four-mvp|access-date=15 May 2016|work=Euroleague.net|date=16 May 2016}}</ref>

On 15 June 2016, De Colo signed a new three-year contract with CSKA.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nando De Colo signed new contract with CSKA|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=15222&lang=en|access-date=15 June 2016|work=cskabasket.com|date=15 June 2016}}</ref> He was named the 2016 [[:fr:All-Europe Player of the Year|All-Europe Player of the Year]] by [[Eurobasket.com]].<ref>[*[https://www.eurobasket.com/European-Awards/basketball_2016.aspx Eurobasket.com European Awards - 2016 Men Basketball].]</ref>
[[File:Nando de Colo 1 PBC CSKA Moscow EuroLeague 20180316 (1).jpg|thumb|upright|De Colo in 2018]]
In May 2018, he was named the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] for the [[2017–18 EuroLeague|2017–18 season]].<ref name="all-euroleague">{{cite news|title=2017-18 All-EuroLeague First Team presented by 7DAYS|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8q8jd3dq5w55m5ab/2017-18-all-euroleague-first-team-presented-by-7days|access-date=19 May 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=10 May 2018}}</ref> On June 9, 2018, he won his third [[VTB United League MVP]] award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/league-announces-individual-awards-at-gala/|title=League Announces Individual Awards At Gala|date=9 June 2018|access-date=10 June 2018|publisher=vtb-league.com}}</ref>

In the 2018–19 season, De Colo won his second EuroLeague title with CSKA after defeating [[Anadolu Efes]] in the championship game of the [[2019 EuroLeague Final Four|Final Four]]. Moscow also went on to win the VTB United League once again, making it his fifth league title.

===Fenerbahçe (2019–2022)===
On July 6, 2019, de Colo signed with [[Fenerbahçe Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball Super League]] and the [[EuroLeague]], on a 2+1 deal.<ref name="euro_Fene">{{Cite web |title=Fenerbahce signed Nando De Colo |website=Eurohoops |date=6 July 2019 |access-date=6 July 2019 |url= https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/903170/fenerbahce-signed-nando-de-colo/}}</ref> On October 19, 2019, de Colo set personal career-high with 39 points in a EuroLeague win over [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Round 3 MVP: Nando De Colo, Fenerbahce |url=https://admin.euroleague.net/news/i/a4lk7hyl3ktdqsgc/round-3-mvp-nando-de-colo-fenerbahce |access-date=19 October 2019 |work=euroleague.net |date=19 October 2019}}</ref> In his first season with the club, he averaged 15.9 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists over 24 EuroLeague games. The season was cut short due to [[COVID-19 pandemic]].

In 2020–21 season, over 32 EuroLeague games, de Colo averaged 15.8 points, 3.9 assists and 3.2 rebounds per game. In December 2021, he suffered a fracture in the [[second metacarpal bone]] of his left hand, which will keep him off the court for weeks after surgery is performed.<ref>{{cite news |title=De Colo diagnosed with metacarpal fracture, Vesely with ligament injury |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1287727/de-colo-diagnosed-with-metacarpal-bone-fracture-vesely-with-ligament-injury-in-ankle/ |access-date=25 December 2021 |work=eurohoops.net |date=24 December 2021}}</ref>

===ASVEL (2022–2025)===
On 30 June 2022, De Colo signed a two-year deal with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-30 |title=Nando de Colo rejoint LDLC ASVEL ! |url=https://ldlcasvel.com/nando-de-colo-rejoint-ldlc-asvel/ |access-date=2022-07-01 |website=LDLC ASVEL |language=fr-FR |archive-date=22 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221022181559/https://ldlcasvel.com/nando-de-colo-rejoint-ldlc-asvel/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Prior to signing he was also talking with [[AS Monaco Basket|Monaco]] and [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nando de Colo names the primary reason why he left Fenerbahce |url=https://basketnews.com/news-175308-nando-de-colo-names-the-primary-reason-why-he-left-fenerbahce.html |access-date=2022-07-17 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

On February 5, 2023, De Colo surpassed [[Nikos Galis]] as the all-time top scorer in European continental basketball competitions with 4,917 points.<ref name=":0" />

On May 17, 2023, De Colo was named to the All-French League Team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-18 |title=Basket. Trophées LNB 2023 : razzia pour Victor Wembanyama, Matt Morgan dans le 5 majeur de la saison |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/basket/le-mans/basket-trophees-lnb-2023-razzia-pour-victor-wembanyama-matt-morgan-dans-le-5-majeur-de-la-saison-73532166-f54a-11ed-9a00-58a9ada1f55a |access-date=2023-05-18 |website=Le Maine Libre |language=fr}}</ref>

===Return to Fenerbahçe (2026)===
On 4 January 2026, de Colo signed a contract with Fenerbahçe until the end of season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-04 |title=Nando De Colo yeniden Fenerbahçe Beko’da! |url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2026/1/nando-de-colo-yeniden-fenerbahce-beko-da |access-date=2026-01-04 |website=Fenerbahce.org |language=tr}}</ref> De Colo ended his career by helping Fenerbahçe win the [[2025–26 Basketbol Süper Ligi]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-20 |title=Nando De Colo ends legendary career with one last title|url=https://basketnews.com/news-250112-nando-de-colo-ends-legendary-career-with-one-last-title.html|access-date=2026-06-20 |website=basketnews.com}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Nando de Colo 2015.jpg|thumbnail|De Colo playing for [[French national basketball team|France]] in 2015]]
De Colo is a regular member of the senior men's [[France national basketball team|French national basketball team]]. He won a silver medal at the [[EuroBasket 2011]] in Lithuania, a gold medal at the [[EuroBasket 2013]] in Slovenia, and a bronze medal at the [[EuroBasket 2015]] in France, where he also earned an [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]] selection.

De Colo played internationally at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 London Olympics]]. He played a major role on the French team during the tournament. He also displayed strong offense and defense, as he scored seven points in their game against the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]].

He was the MVP of the [[2016 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament – Manila|2016 Manila FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]].

In September 2024, De Colo retired from the French National team after the 2024 Paris Olympics via social media.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nando De Colo officially retires from French National Team |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/olympic-games/1719853/nando-de-colo-officially-retires-from-french-national-team/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=11 October 2024 |language=en |date=27 September 2024}}</ref>
